NH4+ cannot accept an electron pair: nitrogen has a complete octet with all four pairs bonding, no lone pair, and no accessible vacant valence orbital. The chapter's OWN definition (6.10.3) is 'a species which accepts electron pair', illustrated with electron-deficient species (BF3, AlCl3, Co3+, Mg2+); NH4+ is not electron deficient. It is a Bronsted acid (proton donor), not a Lewis acid. FLAGGED FOR ADJUDICATION: a minority argument treats NH4+ as a Lewis acid because a base attacks its proton, but that is proton transfer, not electron-pair acceptance by NH4+.
Exact match.
